text:
Global financial markets are bracing for a prolonged period of elevated risk as kinetic conflict in the Middle East escalates, sending crude oil prices surging. Brent crude rose toward $94.85 per barrel following reports of strikes on critical infrastructure, including Kuwait's airport, and consecutive days of U.S. military operations against Iran. This persistent energy supply shock has intensified global inflation fears, prompting the European Central Bank to consider a surprise rate hike, while Indonesia implemented defensive rate hikes and stock buybacks. Tech shares led another sharp Wall Street sell-off as capital fled risk-on assets.

In digital asset markets, Bitcoin is consolidating weakly between $61,000 and $62,000. Although tokenized structural products like BitMart's SpaceX-linked fund draw steady interest, speculative trading has shifted toward prediction markets as the 2026 FIFA World Cup kicks off in North America, prompting U.S. regulators to begin drafting comprehensive compliance frameworks.

Ultimately, these developments show a tightening correlation between traditional macro forces and digital asset behavior. Geopolitical shocks and energy-led rate expectations drive systemic risk-off cycles that depress both traditional equities and cryptocurrencies in tandem. Meanwhile, incoming prediction market regulations and tokenized real-world assets demonstrate that regulatory structures act as direct conduits, formalizing crypto as a highly responsive extension of global monetary conditions.
